provenance_proof: rsijev/arch.py, rsijev/encode.py and rsijev/contract.py are unpatched, and all three git blob shas equal this commit's. That is how the pin was found: by matching bytes, not by trusting a date.
blob_algorithm: git blob sha1 = sha1("blob <len>\0" + bytes), the id `git hash-object` produces
rule: Every file upstream had at the pin must be present here and byte-identical, unless it is listed with a state and a reason. A file that is neither is a defect, not a detail: it means a number in this project was produced by code that is not in this tree.

states.ours: we changed it, and the change is declared
states.added: fetched from upstream main on 2026-10-01, ahead of the pin
states.absent: deliberately not vendored, with the reason given
states.project: this project's own file, with no upstream counterpart

scope.rule: The vendor surface is the running path and nothing wider. A file is vendored because THIS project runs it, cites its numbers, or cannot import without it -- never because it exists upstream.
in: rsijev/* -- the training and evaluation core this project trains and scores with
scripts/suite.py + rsijev/targets_suite.py -- upstream's weighted 15-benchmark mean, which is the answer to a defect this project was hand-rolling around (a bar on one benchmark)
scripts/build_synth_corpus.py + scripts/build_replication_corpus.py -- the corpus, and the record of its bytes
scripts/corpus_gate.py + scripts/build_suite_train_corpus.py -- upstream's decontamination gate, replacing a reimplementation of it
scripts/check_release_records.py -- upstream's path-leak guard, which they record as having failed 13 times
out: the RL2/vision corpus builders (build_rl2_*, build_vision_*, build_depthdial)
release_train.py, routing.py, bench.py -- inference-time and release-time, not search-time
scope.why: Unused vendored code is not free. It has to be kept in step, a broken import in it is a defect this project has to triage, and a large vendored tree implies coverage this project does not have. A narrow vendor surface that is exactly true is worth more than a broad one that is approximately true.
